units.translation: πασσαλευμένος [fastened with pegs] by a corrector. This arose from a gloss προσπεπασσαλευμένος [fastened to] written next to προσπεπαρμένος [pierced through], which I restored, supplied by Aeschylus himself, who in the same sense said προσπαρτός [pierced to] at v. 142: οἵῳ δεσμῷ προσπαρτὸς ἐγώ [to what bond am I pierced?]. In many copies the reading of the Medicean codex is preserved, with only the accent corrected to πασσαλευμένος [fastened with pegs], and with the glosses κεκαρφωμένος [pinned], προσκεκαρφωμένος [pinned to], δεδεμένος [bound], προσηλωμένος [nailed to] added: in others, and partly older ones, among which is the Vossian, πασσαλευτός [fastened with pegs] is written, with one syllable lacking for the integrity of the verse, which Turnebus supplied by adding ὤν [being]. This very thing perhaps the corrector had put who wrote πασσαλευτός [fastened with pegs]. For if he had intended it as a gloss, he would probably have used some participle, like other glossators, rather than the word πασσαλευτός [fastened with pegs], which is read nowhere else.

I suffer: which is said of evils more often than of goods. It is construed with accusatives of either nouns or adjectives.
Without a case
πάσχω [I suffer] joined with adverbs. With κακῶς [badly]
they are said who are affected by good things.
with imperfect ἔπασχον [I was suffering], perfect πέπονθα [I have suffered], aorist ἔπαθον [I suffered], future πείσομαι [I will suffer]
where Schuetz rightly has τάλαν πάθος [wretched suffering].
what shall I suffer? i.e. what will happen to me? or what shall I do? On this see Blomfield in the Glossary on Pers. 909 and Stephanus in Thes. vol. 6 p. 590.
Thus Hermann for γένωμαι [I become] (γελῶμαι [I am laughed at] Tyrwhitt); δύσοιστα πολίταις ἔπαθον [I suffered things hard to bear for the citizens].
